newsitem.title: GERMANY: Magazine adds to speculation Mercedes head to quit.
newsitem.headline: Magazine adds to speculation Mercedes head to quit.

text.p: A German magazine reported on Thursday that the chief executive of Mercedes-Benz AG, Helmut Werner, will quit when the carmaker's parent Daimler-Benz AG implements a planned management reorganisation.

"Manager magazin" reported that Werner's departure was agreed in confidential talks in early December between him, Daimler's management board chairman Juergen Schrempp and supervisory board chairman Hilmar Kopper.

Under the planned revamp Mercedes-Benz AG will be merged into the Daimler-Benz group, a move which Werner reportedly opposes, the magazine said in a summary of an article to be published in its edition on December 20.
Daimler could not immediately be reached for comment but last week denied that any decision had been made.
Schrempp reportedly plans to integrate Mercedes more tightly into the group structure, making it less independent.
Speculation that Werner could step down has intensified in recent weeks, raising the prospect of what would be a serious loss to the company.
Industry analysts have said Werner's departure would be a blow to Mercedes which he guided back to profitability with a massive overhaul in model strategy.
The unsourced report in the magazine said Mercedes, which contributes 70 percent to Daimler's sales, would account for five members on the group's new 10-member management board.

The president of Mercedes-Benz Argentina, Axel Arendt, is likely to become head of personnel at Daimler, taking over from Manfred Gentz who would concentrate exclusively on his responsibilities for finance and controlling, the report said.
Michael Kraemer, head of preliminary research at Mercedes-Benz AG, was the main candidate to replace Hartmut Weule as Daimler's management board member in charge of research, the report said.

Mercedes-Benz management board members Juergen Hubbert, in charge of cars, Kurt Lauk, who heads the truck division, and Dieter Zetsche, who is responsible for marketing and sales, would become ordinary members of the new Daimler management board, the report said.
